labels.label: T-abs-pushup-not-open/line
labels.notes: Causal.jumpLine (PushUpNotOpen.lean:88) is a genuine Causal.Causality ℝ (Causal/Causality.lean:55,77). le U x y := (x = y ∧ x ∈ U) ∨ (x = 0 ∧ y = 1 ∧ 0 ∈ U ∧ 1 ∈ U). This is exactly the target's 'diagonal plus 0 ≤ 1 in every open U containing 0 and 1'. 0 ≤_U 1 needs only 0, 1 ∈ U, not [0,1] ⊆ U, as the target says. lt := False. Every field was checked. le_mem_left/right: the pair disjunct gives 0, 1 ∈ U. le_refl: the diagonal disjunct. le_trans: 0 ≤ 1 ≤ z forces z = 1, and the pair disjunct would need 1 = 0. le_mono: V ≤ U carries 0, 1 ∈ V and x ∈ V to U. lt_mem_*, lt_trans, lt_mono, le_of_lt: vacuous. isOpen_lt_right/left: {y | False} = ∅. jumpLine_le is Iff.rfl. The _of_not lemmas are true: in an open set missing 0 or 1 the order is the diagonal, so J± of V ⊆ U is V. In the library's gluing-free reading (kb/0014) this is a causality, and the SCOPE says so; the reading question is fair (see the separation row).

labels.label: T-abs-pushup-not-open/push-up
labels.notes: jumpLine_pushUp is Causality.PushUp (defi:pushup, Properties.lean:69). It goes through pushUp_iff (Properties.lean:274), and every premise has an lt, which is False. Vacuous, and disclosed as vacuous.

labels.label: T-abs-pushup-not-open/locally-causally-open
labels.notes: jumpLine_locallyCausallyOpen is the two-sided ladder node Causality.LocallyCausallyOpen (LadderLocal.lean:152, = LocallyCausallyOpenFuture ∧ dual.LocallyCausallyOpenFuture), reached through locallyCausallyOpen_iff. The neighbourhoods are {1}ᶜ for x ≠ 1 and {0}ᶜ for x = 1. Each is open and misses 0 or 1, so CausallyOpenFutureOn holds for it and for the dual: every U ≤ W misses 0 or 1, and J⁺_U(V) = J⁻_U(V) = V is open. CausallyOpenFutureOn W is def:causally_open_spacetime_open for W seen as a spacetime (ex:open_subset). The neighbourhoods are open, so the hypothesis also holds if ETT.tex:698's 'neighbourhood' is read as not necessarily open.

labels.label: T-abs-pushup-not-open/not-open
labels.notes: jumpLine_Jplus_Ioo: J⁺_⊤((−1,1)) = (−1,1]. This is correct, since the only off-diagonal pair is 0 ≤ 1 and 0 ∈ (−1,1). The set is not open at 1. jumpLine_not_causallyOpenFuture is the negation of CausallyOpenFuture (Properties.lean:121), which is def:causally_open_spacetime_open as printed, with U = ⊤ and V = (−1,1). The quote of ETT.tex:694 in the docstring is verbatim, without the opening 'Let M be a topological spacetime.'. jumpLine_not_causallyOpen is the DEC-8 two-sided CausallyOpen, through .future.

labels.label: T-abs-pushup-not-open/not-absolutely-minimal
labels.notes: jumpLine_not_absolutelyMinimal is the negation of Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimal (Generated.lean:247, def:topological_space_causality_absolutely), the ladder node's Lean name. It uses causal_ladder (the rule AbsolutelyMinimal.causallyOpenFuture_of_locallyCausallyOpenFuture, LadderLocal.lean:263, after LocallyCausallyOpen.future) and then not_causallyOpenFuture. The direct proof jumpLine_not_absolutelyMinimalOn_top is correct too. In the cover S = {{1}ᶜ, {0}ᶜ} with V = ⊤, each ⊤ ⊓ O misses 0 or 1, so every step of a TransGen chain is an equality, and 0 ≤_ℝ 1 is not such a chain. AbsolutelyMinimal ↔ AbsolutelyMinimalOn ⊤ is Precausality.absolutelyMinimal_iff (Generated.lean:275).

labels.label: T-abs-pushup-not-open/separation
labels.notes: jumpLine_separates_causallyOpenFuture conjoins exactly the twelve listed facts; #check reproduced its type. The docstring quotes prop:topological_spacetime_absolutely_minimal (ETT.tex:698) verbatim, without 'Let M be a topological spacetime.'; the REPORT's range 698-702 includes l.702, which is \begin{proof}, while the prop ends at l.701. not_causallyOpenFuture_of_locallyCausallyOpenFuture_bare (¬∀ C : Causality ℝ, LocallyCausallyOpenFuture → CausallyOpenFuture) refutes exactly the proposition without absolute minimality, as printed (one-sided). not_causallyOpen_of_locallyCausallyOpen_bare refutes it in the DEC-8 two-sided reading. Both refutations hold over ℝ, which is a topological spacetime (T2, second countable). The hypothesis uses open neighbourhoods, so the refutation also covers the reading with non-open neighbourhoods. The _pushUp_ form adds push-up to the hypotheses. The Lean statements are about the library's Causality and are true. Whether they refute the paper depends on the reading of defi:causalite, and the module SCOPE discloses this. The reading question is fair. defi:causalite (ETT.tex:237-251) says 'sheaf with values in C' and states no gluing axiom; the 'Equivalently' form (a)-(c) is what the library carries. OQ-18 (DECISIONS.md:174, OPEN) itself identifies gluing with '≤ generated by covers, i.e. absolute minimality'. Under that reading every causality is absolutely minimal. Then prop 698 (in Lean: AbsolutelyMinimal.causallyOpenFuture_of_locallyCausallyOpenFuture) gives local ⇒ global causal openness, and no witness of this separation can exist. The structure is the same as OQ-39 (deuxPushup). The REPORT says correctly that push_up ⇏ causally_open_future holds in both readings: Causal.rationalLine_separates_absolutelyMinimal (NestedConverse.lean:394) is absolutely minimal, push-up, and not causally open in the future. No ETT label is marked, so the ETT ledger cannot misread this as certification of a paper statement.

labels.label: T-abs-pushup-not-open/beyond
labels.notes: Each claim was checked against its definition. IsCausal (Properties.lean:95): 1 ≤ 0 holds nowhere. Every diamond J(p,q) ⊆ {p,q}: if p ≤ x ≤ q is off the diagonal, then p = 0, x = 1 and x ≤ q forces q = 1. GloballyHyperbolic (:144): causal with finite, hence compact, diamonds. StronglyCausalOpen (:109): every subset is causally convex in ⊤, and interior U is open. HasTimeFunction (CurvesExtend.lean:516): T = id with 0 < 1. Not ChronalNeighbours: lt is False. Not Tarentin: an open diamond containing 0 would contain an infinite Ioo inside the finite set {p,q}. Not CausallyPlain: Int J⁺_⊤(ℝ) = ℝ while closure I⁺ = ∅. Not CausallyArcConnected: through CausallyArcConnected.absolutelyMinimal (ArcConnected.lean:216). These are beyond the target and disclosed as such. The ladder ids in the for_keeper entries all match the Lean names in programme/ladder.toml [[property]]: push_up, locally_causally_open, globally_hyperbolic, strongly_causal_open, time_function, causally_open_future, absolutely_minimal, chronal_neighbours, tarentin, causally_plain.

findings.what: The declaration docstrings of not_causallyOpenFuture_of_locallyCausallyOpenFuture_bare and not_causallyOpen_of_locallyCausallyOpen_bare say '`prop:topological_spacetime_absolutely_minimal` without absolute minimality ... is false', with no qualifier. The module SCOPE discloses this, so the Lean statements and the marks are fine. The sentence is likely to be quoted on its own, for example in the keeper's ladder.toml comment.
